prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single universally “best” company — the best choice depends on the neighborhood, your roof type, scope of work, and who can prove they install Miami‑Dade/Florida Building Code hurricane‑rated systems correctly. Instead of one name, use a checklist and selection process that reliably identifies a top contractor for hurricane‑rated replacement.

How to find the right contractor
- Verify license and insurance
  - Confirm the contractor is properly licensed with the Florida DBPR (search at myfloridalicense.com).
  - Ask for current general liability and workers’ compensation certificates that name you as an additional insured during the job.
- Confirm Miami‑Dade / Florida product approvals
  - For hurricane-rated materials and assemblies ask for the Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval for the materials & assembly they intend to use.
- Look for manufacturer certifications
  - Prefer contractors who are certified installers (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, TAMKO Pro, etc.). These certifications mean training and enhanced warranties.
- Check experience and references
  - Ask how many hurricane-rated roofs they’ve installed in Miami, and request recent local references and photos.
  - Check Google/Yelp reviews and BBB rating and complaint history.
- Ask specific technical questions
  - What wind rating (mph) will your system be designed for?
  - Will they pull permits and handle inspections?
  - What underlayment, flashing, fastener schedule, and deck attachment will be used? Request the NOA numbers or manufacturer details for each.
  - What warranty is provided (labor, workmanship, manufacturer), and is it transferable?
- Get multiple written bids
  - Obtain at least 3 detailed proposals (scope, materials with brand/model, fastener type and spacing, ventilation, removal vs. overlay, disposal, timeline, total cost).
- Red flags
  - High-pressure sales, demand for huge deposits (typically 10–30% is normal), no contract or verbal-only agreements, lack of local references, or inability to produce licenses/NOAs/insurance.

Where to look
- Search for Miami‑based contractors that are:
  - Miami‑Dade NOA/Florida approved installers
  - Manufacturer‑certified (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning)
  - Highly rated locally with verifiable references
- Use DBPR, Miami‑Dade County building department, and manufacturer locator tools to find certified installers.

If you want, I can:
- Look up manufacturer‑certified or Miami‑Dade NOA installers near your address or ZIP code (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood).
- Draft a short RFP/email you can send to multiple contractors to compare bids.

Which option would you like?
